business_problem: Beamable needed a backend platform that could give game developers scalable identity, commerce, social, and live-operations services without forcing them to build or manage the underlying data infrastructure themselves.
solution_summary: Beamable standardized its game-development platform on MongoDB Atlas so it could provide developers with ready-to-use backend capabilities for identity, commerce, social systems, inventories, and live operations. The company supports both multi-tenant and single-tenant deployments, so it needed horizontal and vertical scale, very low-latency reads and writes, and a data model flexible enough to accommodate custom cloud code and customer-specific extensions. Atlas became the core document platform behind Beamable's managed services and private-cloud product, while AWS Fargate and broader AWS infrastructure host the surrounding runtime. The team chose MongoDB because document inserts performed well, sharding enabled large-scale multi-tenant workloads, and the platform avoided painful migrations as customer data models evolved. This lets Beamable absorb spiky launch traffic, avoid glue code, and give development teams a faster route from prototype to live game operations.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the identity, gameplay, social, commerce, and cloud-code data that powers Beamable's live-operations platform.

solution_components.name: AWS Fargate
solution_components.role: Runs the managed compute layer that hosts Beamable services around the Atlas-backed data platform.

data_flow: Game clients and Beamable's developer tooling send identity, inventory, social, commerce, and cloud-code events into Beamable services, those services persist and query the data in MongoDB Atlas, and the platform returns live-operational state to both Beamable operators and end-user games in near real time.
business_outcome: Beamable cut time and cost for game studios, handled large traffic bursts more easily, and created a reusable backend platform that lets developers focus on content, monetization, and strategy instead of infrastructure.
metrics: Beamable supports 35+ games currently live, 60+ in active development, and 100+ going through tech evaluation.
Launch traffic can reach around 14,000 requests per second.
The platform handles billions of API calls per month.
Beamable can save some development teams USD $300,000-400,000 each year and cut up to four months from a one-year development cycle.
architecture_clues: Beamable supports both multi-tenant and single-tenant offerings on the same general architecture.
Sharded MongoDB data models are used to scale high-throughput game workloads.
Cloud code executes sensitive multiplayer logic on the server side.
